id: I Know What You Did Last Summer (1997)
title: I Know What You Did Last Summer
tagline: He's got a hook on them...
about: A year after four friends dump a man they ran over on a coast road, someone in a fisherman's slicker starts sending notes and swinging a hook.
cue: Serve the fish when Helen is crowned at the Croaker pageant.
faces: HE'S GOT A HOOK ON THEM...

    StartersCar boot crab cakes with remouladeJulie finds crabs all over Max. Golden blue swimmer crab cakes and lemon.How to make it400g blue swimmer crab meat, picked60g panko breadcrumbs, plus 60g for coating1 egg3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise, plus 125g for the remoulade1 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp Old Bay or seafood seasoning2 spring onions, finely sliced1 tbsp capers, chopped2 small gherkins, chopped2 tbsp vegetable oil1 lemonMix the crab, 60g panko, egg, 3 tbsp mayo, mustard, seasoning and spring onions without breaking up the crab too much.Shape into 8 small cakes, press into the rest of the panko and chill for 10 minutes.Fry in the oil until golden, about 3 minutes a side.Stir the capers and gherkins through the rest of the mayo with a squeeze of lemon and serve alongside.Southport hush puppies with honey butterRay now works the fishing boats. Crisp cornmeal bites and whipped honey butter.How to make it150g fine cornmeal75g self-raising flour1 tbsp caster sugar1 egg185ml buttermilk1/2 small brown onion, grated1 L vegetable oil, for frying100g butter, softened2 tbsp honeyWhisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar and a pinch of salt, then stir in the egg, buttermilk and onion to a thick batter.Drop teaspoonfuls into oil at 180°C and fry until deep golden, in batches.Beat the butter with the honey and a pinch of salt and serve with the hot hush puppies.Salt and vinegar chips by the scoopAngela Lansbury always had a plan.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsCroaker Queen fried whiting and chipsHelen is crowned Croaker Queen. Cornmeal-crusted whiting and thick-cut chips.How to make it600g whiting fillets1kg floury potatoes, cut in thick chips1.5 L vegetable oil, for frying125ml buttermilk100g fine cornmeal50g plain flour1 tsp Old Bay or seafood seasoning125g tartare sauce2 lemonsFry the chips at 150°C until soft but pale, then drain.Dip the whiting in buttermilk, then in the cornmeal, flour and seasoning.Raise the oil to 185°C and fry the fish until crisp and golden, then drain.Fry the chips again until crisp and salt them.Serve with tartare sauce and lemon wedges.Billy Blue prawns and gritsRay's boat is called the Billy Blue. Garlic butter prawns over cheesy grits.How to make it750g green king prawns, peeled180g polenta or quick grits750ml milk100g cheddar, grated60g butter3 garlic cloves, sliced1 tsp smoked paprika3 spring onions, sliced1 lemonBring the milk and 250ml water to a simmer, whisk in the grits and cook, stirring, until thick and soft.Stir in the cheddar and half the butter and season.Fry the garlic in the rest of the butter, add the prawns and paprika and cook until pink.Spoon the grits into bowls, top with the prawns and pan butter, spring onions and a squeeze of lemon.SweetsFourth of July banana pudding cupsBarry and Helen at the Fourth of July parade. Vanilla custard, banana and wafer layers.How to make it500ml milk3 egg yolks80g caster sugar2 tbsp cornflour1 tsp vanilla extract3 ripe bananas, sliced150g vanilla wafer biscuits200ml thickened cream, whippedWhisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour, then whisk in the hot milk and stir over the heat until thick.Stir in the vanilla and cool with baking paper on the surface.Layer wafers, banana and custard in 4 cups, twice over.Top with whipped cream and a crumbled wafer.DrinksYellow slicker rum punchA fisherman in a slicker with a hook. Golden rum, pineapple, orange and lime.How to make it160ml golden rum300ml pineapple juice200ml orange juice2 limes2 tbsp grenadine2 cups ice cubesStir the rum, pineapple and orange juice and the juice of 1 lime in a jug.Pour over ice, drip a little grenadine down each glass and add a lime wheel.Carolina sweet teaBrewed hot, sugared, then poured over ice.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
